body.en:
Question B-002-009-001.

Why the correct answer is right: A QSL card is written proof that two amateur radio operators made a contact.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "A notice of an apparent infraction from Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada": An infraction notice from Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) is an enforcement document, not a QSL confirmation.
- sourceIndex 2: "A postcard reminding you when your certificate will expire": Certificate-expiry reminders are licensing administration, not proof of a radio contact.
- sourceIndex 3: "A letter or postcard from an amateur radio operator": A generic letter or postcard is not necessarily proof unless it confirms the communication details.
